observations.summary: The window defines surface normalization before deterministic strategy selection.
Yolo requires DAE, while DAE eligibility can be denied and silent HTE downgrade is prohibited.
An accepted PlanUnit explicitly preserves implementation-blocking runtime-governance gaps.
Concurrency and run-envelope defaults provide concrete numeric values.
Kill, terminal, shutdown, and crash-recovery concepts are named, but their complete cross-trigger transition protocol is not present in the window.
The listed validation surfaces exercise plan migration and indexing rather than executable runtime behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Execution escalation authority is unspecified
candidate_findings.claim: Regular, yolo, and Debug+yolo postures are defined, but the window does not identify which caller or role may select or transition into full automation, whether mid-run escalation is legal, or what consent artifact must be persisted.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An ambiguous escalation boundary can let a UI, provider, resumed run, or stale request acquire materially broader execution authority without attributable authorization.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define authorized callers and roles, a fail-closed mode-transition state machine, explicit yolo confirmation and revocation rules, handling of pending approvals during transition, and persisted actor, policy revision, and consent evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Yolo has no defined outcome when DAE is unavailable
candidate_findings.claim: The strategy function selects DAE for yolo, provider policy may make DAE unselectable, and yolo may not silently downgrade to HTE, but no rejection state, stop reason, retry path, or user recovery action is defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The unsatisfied combination can produce implementation-specific fallback, late dispatch failure, misleading GUI state, or partial work before rejection.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify pre-dispatch eligibility evaluation, a stable typed rejection or terminal reason, zero-side-effect guarantees, GUI explanation and allowed recovery actions, and deterministic reselection behavior after provider or policy change.

candidate_findings.title: DAE containment does not bound reads, secrets, network, or escape paths
candidate_findings.claim: DAE is described as a jail or worktree that blocks canonical-workspace writes, while the gap register still names DAE isolation and external-publish side effects; the window does not constrain canonical reads, environment and credential inheritance, network egress, symlink or submodule escape, or provider-side publication.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A Git worktree is not itself a security sandbox, so a delegated provider could exfiltrate secrets, mutate external systems, or reach the canonical tree through paths not covered by the direct-write prohibition.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the jail capability matrix, filesystem roots and link resolution, secret and environment scrubbing, network and external-publish policy, subprocess inheritance, denial telemetry, and adversarial escape tests for every supported platform.

candidate_findings.title: DAE reconciliation lacks atomicity and crash semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The jail diff becomes authoritative and reconciliation follows scans and FileSafe checks, but conflict detection, source revision binding, all-or-nothing application, rollback, idempotent replay, and crash handling for an unreconciled jail are unspecified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent canonical edits or a crash between scan and apply can lose user work, apply a stale diff, duplicate changes, or leave an ambiguous run outcome.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Bind each diff and scan result to immutable base and destination revisions; define conflict and attention states, transactional apply and rollback, replay keys, durable reconciliation checkpoints, and resume, discard, and cleanup authority.

candidate_findings.title: Mutable policy inputs undermine pure strategy selection
candidate_findings.claim: Strategy selection is called a pure function of config and policy, but the window does not define immutable input snapshots, version identifiers, precedence, evaluation time, or whether an in-flight run is re-evaluated after policy or account changes.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent configuration or policy mutation can make identical requests resolve differently and make persisted strategy reasons impossible to reproduce or audit.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a complete typed input record with config, provider-policy, permission, account, and overlay revisions; deterministic precedence and unknown-value behavior; snapshot timing; persistence for every run; and explicit re-evaluation rules.

candidate_findings.title: Accepted gap register has no closure contracts
candidate_findings.claim: RM-013 is accepted while explicitly preserving implementation-blocking gaps, has no negative constraints, and uses preservation-oriented acceptance criteria rather than per-gap resolution criteria.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The PlanUnit can pass governance validation while startup recovery, account invalidation, external side effects, blocked semantics, and other named blockers remain non-buildable and non-testable.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Represent each gap with an owner and authority, input and output schema, state transitions, failure behavior, target owner document, dependency and closure state, negative constraints, and deterministic acceptance oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime authority truth has no propagation protocol
candidate_findings.claim: Surface states map to runtime modes and recovery surfaces use allowed_action_ids[], but the window does not define a single authoritative UI payload, update ordering, stale-response rejection, unknown-action handling, or how normalized mode, strategy, and yolo authority remain visibly synchronized.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A surface can display regular or read-only posture while the runtime executes yolo or DAE, or can expose recovery actions no longer permitted by current policy.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the authoritative presentation payload and revision, subscription and refresh events, fail-closed behavior for unknown or stale IDs, explicit yolo and DAE indicators, disabled reasons, and cross-surface propagation tests.

candidate_findings.title: Global caps lack atomic admission and durable queue semantics
candidate_findings.claim: Three concurrency defaults and a no-discard rule are stated, but counting scope, atomic admission across supervisors or processes, queue ordering and fairness, cancellation and timeout behavior, leases, crash recovery, and observability are absent.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Racing dispatchers can exceed limits; queued work can starve, survive cancellation, or disappear after restart; and operators cannot reconcile the stated caps with active capacity.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define which states and actors consume each counter, the global coordination authority and atomic reservation protocol, durable queue schema, priority and fairness, cancellation and expiration, lease recovery, overload behavior, and queue and cap metrics.

candidate_findings.title: Budget fields lack measurement and aggregation semantics
candidate_findings.claim: Budget values are enumerated and frozen across pause/resume, but the window does not define counter scope, units and clocks, whether paused time counts, child-run aggregation, concurrent updates, retry resets, token-estimation authority, write-window calculation, warning emission, or the actual hard ceilings.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Independent implementations can enforce materially different limits, overspend shared budgets, reset counters on resume, or terminate runs inconsistently.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define every counter's unit, authoritative producer, inclusion rules, monotonic update and child roll-up algorithm, pause/resume and retry behavior, overflow handling, hard-ceiling source, warning event cardinality, and deterministic boundary fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Kill triggers and terminal outcomes lack a total transition table
candidate_findings.claim: The window distinguishes kill.* triggers from done.* outcomes and specifies special budget handling, but it does not map every trigger to a terminal state, define precedence for concurrent timeout, signal, budget, tool, and persistence failures, or guarantee exactly-once durable completion.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Races can produce contradictory terminal events, duplicate completion, lost usage, or a stop reason that varies with scheduling rather than policy.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide the complete trigger-to-terminal mapping, precedence and tie-break rules, atomic ordering of cancellation, usage flush, stop-reason persistence, and terminal emission, idempotency keys, and recovery behavior when durable recording fails.

candidate_findings.title: Doom-loop identity is not reproducibly defined
candidate_findings.claim: The guard depends on serialized_args_hash, exact error_message equality, nesting level, and consecutive attempts, but no canonical serializer, hash algorithm or version, byte and Unicode rules, redaction rule, concurrency scope, or explicit binding to max_same_shell_failure=3 is provided.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-platform serialization differences or nondeterministic error text can prevent the guard from firing, while unredacted errors or unstable hashes can leak data or make replay incompatible.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify canonical argument serialization and hash version, error comparison bytes and redaction, nesting and consecutive-attempt scope under parallel execution, reset conditions, collision handling, and the exact threshold field consumed by the guard.

candidate_findings.title: Shutdown and startup recovery lack an executable protocol
candidate_findings.claim: Idempotent shutdown, durability flushing, process teardown, and done.crashed synthesis are required, but deadlines, escalation order, resource dependencies, repeated-signal behavior, multi-starter ownership, resumable-run classification, and exactly-once crash recovery are not defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A hung child or competing startup can block shutdown, close storage before terminal persistence, emit duplicate done.crashed records, or incorrectly destroy resumable queued or DAE work.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the shutdown and recovery state machines, per-platform signal escalation and deadlines, ordered resource graph, durable checkpoints, recovery lease or leader election, idempotency key, resumability rules, and tests for crash points and repeated signals.

candidate_findings.title: HTE tool-use detection boundary is underspecified
candidate_findings.claim: Provider-originated tool_use is an immediate kill condition, but the window does not define normalized equivalents across providers, partial or malformed stream fragments, duplicate observations, buffered events after cancellation, or the race between observation and possible side effects.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Adapters can disagree about what constitutes the first tool-use event or continue processing after kill, weakening the no-side-effect guarantee.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the provider-neutral detector schema, incremental parsing boundary, malformed and duplicate handling, atomic cancel-and-discard sequence, post-kill stream policy, safe persistence and redaction, and provider fixture corpus.

candidate_findings.title: Accepted runtime requirements have no executable conformance oracles
candidate_findings.claim: Representative strategy, terminal-reason, and crash-recovery PlanUnits list only plan-migration and index validators, with no deterministic runtime tests for their behavioral contracts.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Governance can pass while strategy resolution, terminal ordering, cancellation, recovery, isolation, and budget enforcement remain incorrect or unimplemented.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Add deterministic decision-table tests, failure-injection and crash-point suites, concurrency and idempotency tests, platform signal fixtures, jail-escape tests, persisted-event assertions, and GUI propagation fixtures tied to each PlanUnit acceptance criterion.

candidate_findings.title: Retired caps and stop reasons lack versioned migration behavior
candidate_findings.claim: The window retires 5-crew/10-agent wording and consumer-facing kill.task_timeout, but does not specify accepted schema versions, rewrite versus reject behavior, treatment of stored envelopes and historical events, or telemetry for legacy producers.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Old clients and persisted runs may be silently reinterpreted, rejected inconsistently, or surfaced with conflicting terminal and concurrency semantics.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define version gates, read-time and write-time migration, immutable historical-display rules, legacy alias normalization, warning and rejection telemetry, and compatibility fixtures for every supported producer and stored schema version.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Yolo is explicitly bounded by permissions, FileSafe, provider constraints, prompt-pipeline constraints, and child-capability narrowing.
HTE explicitly prohibits delegated tool execution and assigns provider tool_use a terminal kill contract.
DAE explicitly forbids direct canonical-workspace writes and disallows providers lacking deterministic pre-spawn restrictions.
Named GUI surface states are explicitly normalized and Interview, BrainStorm, and Crew are prohibited from creating new runtime modes.
The concurrency and run-envelope defaults are numerically specified, and queued work may not be silently discarded or auto-widened.
Pre-dispatch and post-response budget outcomes are explicitly distinguished, and kill.task_timeout is explicitly retired as a consumer-facing alias.
Fuzzy, substring, and looks-similar matching are explicitly prohibited for the identical-failure guard.
Incomplete runs may not be silently dropped or rewritten as done.failed without a crash marker, and teardown resources are enumerated in adjacent context.

unknowns.question: Do referenced owner documents define the missing mode-transition, kill-precedence, queue, budget, and reconciliation state machines?
unknowns.reason: Those documents were outside the allowed inputs and could not be inspected.

unknowns.question: What exact externally visible result is required when yolo is requested from a provider with dae_allowed=false?
unknowns.reason: The window prohibits both DAE selection and silent HTE downgrade without naming the remaining transition.

unknowns.question: Is a DAE worktree always wrapped in an OS-enforced sandbox, or can worktree isolation stand alone?
unknowns.reason: The authorized text permits a jail or worktree but does not define their security equivalence.

unknowns.question: Are config, policy, permission, provider, and account revisions captured in a universal run-start record outside this window?
unknowns.reason: Only the Debug PlanUnit explicitly names a persisted run.started snapshot.

unknowns.question: Are executable conformance suites linked elsewhere to these PlanUnits?
unknowns.reason: The visible validation_surfaces contain only plan migration and index validation.

unknowns.question: Where are the hard policy ceilings above the listed budget defaults defined, and which authority may change them?
unknowns.reason: The window references hard ceilings without enumerating or versioning them.

unknowns.question: Which legacy schema and client versions must accept retired concurrency wording and kill.task_timeout?
unknowns.reason: Retirement is stated without a compatibility interval or migration matrix.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: canonical_text: "regular is the standard execution posture with normal approvals; yolo is the full-automation execution posture, still bounded by permissions, FileSafe, provider, and prompt-pipeline constraints."
negative_constraints: ["yolo does not bypass child capability narrowing, provider restrictions, or FileSafe guardrails."]

canonical_text: "Hosted Tool Execution keeps provider CLIs in plan/reasoner and no-side-effect posture while Puppet Master owns every real action through its tools, permissions, FileSafe stack, and hosted action loop; provider tool_use in HTE is a kill condition."

canonical_text: "Delegated Agent Execution runs provider tools inside an isolated PM-managed jail or worktree context, records worktree identity in execution context, treats jail diff as authoritative, blocks direct canonical-workspace writes, requires dae_allowed policy, and reconciles only after scans and FileSafe checks."

negative_constraints: ["The canonical workspace MUST NOT be directly writable during DAE.", "Providers that cannot offer deterministic pre-spawn restriction / tool-policy injection MUST advertise dae_allowed = false and cannot be selected for DAE."]

canonical_text: "Surface states normalize to runtime mode before strategy selection: Ask to ask, Plan and Deep Plan to plan, Agent/Debug/Interview/BrainStorm/Crew standard approvals to regular, and explicit YOLO posture to yolo."
negative_constraints: ["Interview, BrainStorm, and Crew MUST NOT create additional runtime mode values."]

canonical_text: "Strategy selection is a deterministic pure function of requested runtime mode, effective overlay, config, and policy: ask/plan always HTE, regular defaults HTE unless DAE is requested and allowed, and yolo selects DAE."
negative_constraints: ["Given the same inputs, the same strategy MUST be selected.", "regular must not select DAE unless config requests it and provider policy allows it."]

canonical_text: "Debug is a workflow overlay plus target/evidence package, not a new runtime mode; automated Debug cannot execute in read-only mode, defaults to regular+HTE, treats yolo as explicit opt-in, and persists overlay, mode, strategy, reason, and active Debug Automation Profile snapshot in run.started."

negative_constraints: ["Debug with mode ask or plan is an invalid automated-debug combination.", "Debug Mode + yolo is an advanced opt-in only and MUST NOT become the default Debug posture.", "yolo still requires DAE and MUST NOT silently downgrade to HTE."]

canonical_text: "The P5 run-mode recovery section preserves implementation-blocking governance gaps around startup recovery, retry/backoff ownership, Contribute(PR) versus DAE isolation, DAE jail durability, external publish side effects, /event recovery, attention_required persistence, blocked semantics, account-switch invalidation, child-run account re-resolution, gate placement, and work-item posture."
negative_constraints: []

acceptance_criteria: ["RM-013 remains addressable as a fine-grained Run Modes PlanUnit with source-span coverage.", "ContractRefs, anchors or aliases, exact tokens, negative constraints, compatibility notes, stale/retired dispositions, owner boundaries, and source lineage from the source spans remain preserved.", "No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, production build tasks, implementation files, or source code are created by this PlanUnit."]
unit_type: "requirement", status: "accepted"

canonical_text: "Runtime recovery and explanation surfaces must converge on canonical allowed_action_ids[] and explanation-depth controls; unstable UI labels are warning examples, and ELI5/Expert changes simplify explanation depth without renaming canonical object names such as Feature Seam."

canonical_text: "Global run-strategy concurrency defaults are max_concurrent_crews_per_platform=4, max_concurrent_agents_per_crew=8, and max_total_active_agents=32; Persona or overlay configuration alone must not override them, and stale 5-crew/10-agent wording is retired."

negative_constraints: ["Three-level concurrency limits apply globally across all run strategies and MUST NOT be overridden by Persona or overlay configuration alone.", "PM MUST NOT silently discard or auto-widen queued work."]

canonical_text: "Run supervisors enforce canonical run-envelope budget fields across strategies, freezing them into the envelope across pause/resume: max_nesting_depth=4, max_total_spawned_agents=99, max_tool_rounds=200, max_wall_ms=1200000, max_estimated_tokens=80000, max_same_shell_failure=3, max_write_thrashing=5 writes/10 min, max_retryable_errors=3, inherited task_timeout_ms, and warn_budget_pct=80."
negative_constraints: ["Budget overrides MAY narrow defaults per run, but MUST NOT widen beyond the hard policy ceiling.", "task_timeout_ms may narrow parent budget but MUST NOT exceed it."]

canonical_text: "Run kill enforcement distinguishes pre-dispatch/supervisor kill.* triggers from terminal done.* outcomes, persists canonical stop reasons, retires consumer-facing kill.task_timeout, and keeps post-response budget overrun as done.budget_exceeded after usage is durably recorded."

negative_constraints: ["kill.budget_exceeded remains pre-dispatch only.", "Post-response budget-overrun cases MUST NOT be folded back into pre-dispatch kill.budget_exceeded.", "kill.task_timeout is retired as a consumer-facing terminal alias."]

canonical_text: "The doom-loop guard compares only the same tool_name, serialized_args_hash, and error_message triple at the same nesting level across consecutive attempts; fuzzy, substring, or looks-similar matching is prohibited and broader retry suppression belongs to Tools."

canonical_text: "PM entrypoints own shutdown signal fan-out, process group isolation, platform-specific teardown, idempotent shutdown, durability flushing, cancellation outcome mapping, and startup crash recovery that synthesizes done.crashed with crash_recovered metadata instead of silently dropping unfinished runs."
negative_constraints: ["PM MUST NOT silently drop an incomplete run or rewrite it as done.failed without the crash marker."]

canonical_text: "Runtime teardown deterministically closes DB handles, MCP sessions, terminal shells, temporary files, and subprocess groups, emits diagnostics for failed teardown, mints new helper identity after restart, and monitors long-lived helper memory pressure for controlled restart or failover."
